varieties.text:
Mammoth-Sandwich Island

A white-skinned salsify grown for long roots with a mild flavour. Sold under several Mammoth and Sandwich Island names.

Long Black Maxima (scorzonera)

A scorzonera with long, black-skinned roots and pale flesh. A distinct crop from white-rooted salsify.

text:
Salsify & Scorzonera.
DIFFICULTY
Fairly Easy
2/5
HARVEST SEASONS
Spring / Autumn / Winter

Salsify and scorzonera are related but distinct root crops, grown for delicacy rather than bulk. Thin, brittle roots are awkward to lift and clean, so usable yields may be modest. Creamy-rooted salsify, the “vegetable oyster”, has a delicate oyster-like flavour; scorzonera is black-skinned. Both need deep, friable soil and direct sowing, and withstand most winter weather. Roots left for a second season may flower attractively; young flower stalks are edible before they toughen.

Quick facts
Sow

Salsify Mar–May. Jun gives smaller roots. Scorzonera Mar–Apr.

Harvest

Oct – Mar

Germination

14–21 days

Ready in

About 25 weeks from sowing; lift from autumn through winter

Sowing depth

Salsify: 1/2 in.; scorzonera: see packet.

Row spacing

Salsify: 12 in.; scorzonera: see packet.

Plant spacing

Salsify: thin to 4 in.; scorzonera: see packet.

Yield (10 ft row)

About 4 lb; usable yield may be small

Recommended varieties
Mammoth-Sandwich Island

A white-skinned salsify grown for long roots with a mild flavour. Sold under several Mammoth and Sandwich Island names.

Long Black Maxima (scorzonera)

A scorzonera with long, black-skinned roots and pale flesh. A distinct crop from white-rooted salsify.

Duplex (scorzonera)

A productive scorzonera with long, dark-skinned roots and a delicate flavour.

Key risks
White blister

Pale spots develop white spore pustules, often beneath the leaves.

Forked roots

Stones, compaction, fresh manure and damage to the young taproot can cause forking.

Snapped roots

Long, brittle roots break when pulled against firm or sticky soil.

Bolting

Premature flowering can reduce the root crop.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
82
ROOT CROPS

Give the long roots good soil.

Deep, friable ground makes straight growth and careful lifting easier.

Grow for flavour rather than bulk.

These tender, slender roots give a modest but distinctive winter crop.

Soil & preparation
Choose deep, stone-free, friable soil for straight roots and lifting without breakage. Sandy/light loams are easier to clean.
Prepare deeply in autumn/winter, using previously enriched ground. On heavy clay, try a deep raised bed or container. Avoid fresh manure.
Give a fine, open seedbed; avoid heavy feeding or fresh/lumpy material before sowing.
Sowing & planting
Sow salsify
Thin in place
Salsify 

Sow thinly in drills ½ in. deep in the final bed. Disturbed roots seldom grow straight, so discard the thinnings.

Scorzonera 

Sow in place too, following the depth and spacing for the named variety. The illustrations and salsify measurements apply to the pale-rooted crop.

Looking after the crop
Thin salsify carefully to 4 in. apart. Follow the seed packet for scorzonera.
Keep young plants free of weeds. Hand-weed near the crowns; hoes can damage the narrow roots.
Water during dry weather and mulch light soils in summer or autumn where useful.
Foliage may die back in winter, but hardy roots can remain in the ground while lifting is practical.
Harvesting & storage
Lift worthwhile roots from mid-autumn. Cold improves flavour; sound roots stand much of winter. Long, slender roots are normal: no minimum thickness is needed.
Loosen soil deeply; ease brittle roots out gently. Pulling against firm ground breaks them, making cleaning and storage harder.
Lift a supply before the soil freezes. In very cold areas, store in damp sand in a cool, frost-free shed/cellar. Scorzonera can grow larger in year two; lift salsify in its first winter, before flowering reduces root quality.
Pests & diseases
Problem	What to look for	What to do
White blister	White leaf blisters; growth is checked.	Remove affected leaves and debris; avoid crowding.
Forked roots	Long roots divide into forks.	Avoid stones, compaction and fresh manure.
Snapped roots	Brittle roots break during lifting.	Loosen soil deeply and lift gently.
Bolting	Flower stems form before useful roots.	Follow variety sowing dates; avoid checks to growth.
Small roots	Roots too small to use.	Allow a full season. Thin, weed and water in dry spells.
Final tips

Discard thinnings rather than transplanting: disturbed taproots rarely make a good crop.

Scorzonera can be grown on into a second year; salsify left too long will flower and seed.

Young second-year flower shoots can be cut and eaten before they become hard.

Grow these crops for delicacy and flavour rather than expecting a bulky staple yield.

VEGETABLE GUIDES
83
ROOT CROPS
